name: Malcolm
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Meng Chong' was fully localized to 'Malcolm', a hard-sounding Western name suiting his menacing antagonist role; his faction, the source Devil Race, is rendered as the Ogres in the adaptation.
description: Malcolm is the Ogre seat holder in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 597-680) who publicly declares a death sentence on Zane and schemes to have him killed. In the source he is Meng Chong, the representative of the Devil Race's Flame Demon and Fear Demon Holy Lands, who waits for Luo Zheng to leave the Innate Stele before moving against him and even offers ten saint artifacts as a bounty on his life. He is contemptuous, sinister, and politically powerful among the seat holders, exchanging schemes with Fabian and Jarrod. His episode range and prominence align almost exactly with Meng Chong's chapter range (582-679).

name: Eastern Territory
issues: Episodes alternate between singular 'Eastern Territory' (32 mentions) and plural 'Eastern Territories' (51 mentions) for the same region; the sheet should fix one display form.
reason: The source region 'Eastern Region' (also translated 'Eastern Domain') was localized as 'Eastern Territory' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: The Eastern Territory is the home region of Zane Lowell and House Lowell, the setting of the early story (Eps 1 onward) and the location of the Skyreach Sect. It is a relatively weak frontier of the human world: its craftsmen are renowned but its cultivation methods are provincial compared to the Heartlands, and its humans fought back against demonic invasions, even killing several Netherlords. It corresponds to the source novel's Eastern Region/Eastern Domain, where the Luo Clan ranks low in the overall hierarchy. The region remains a reference point throughout the show, with characters like Isla Novak and the Shadow Group tied to its history.

name: Relic-Class
reason: The source term 'Sacred Artifact' was localized as 'Relic-Class', slotting it into the show's numbered weapon-tier ladder (Tier 6, above Divine Arms) for consistency with the Western fantasy register.
description: Relic-Class is the sixth and highest regular weapon tier in the show's equipment ladder, sitting above Divine Arms (Tier 5) and below nothing else known in the Heartlands era; such items are extremely rare. Known Relic-Class items include the Nameless Saber (Maddox), the Ethereal Spirit Sect's Soul Flag, the World Merchants' Guild's Time Copper Coin, the Heavenly Feather Crown, and the Dragonfall Palace Armor. The tier debuts around Ep 492, when Zane stuns onlookers by gifting Tia a Relic-Class protective armor that outshines the two secret Relic-Class weapons in the Guild's own vault. It corresponds to the source novel's 'Sacred Artifact' (saint artifact), the treasure class that defines a sect's standing.

name: Ingrid
issues: Historical split: Eps 201-208 mistakenly called this character 'Helen' (a different, real Helen of House Solomon also exists); per the master sheet this was corrected, and 'Ingrid' is canonical.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhu Qianning' was fully localized to 'Ingrid', a distinctive Western name for the needle-wielding young woman of the Blackwood Clan; her source family, the Zhu Family famed for needle techniques, became the Blackwood Clan.
description: Ingrid is a young woman of the Blackwood Clan, a family famous for their deadly Throwing Needles, and the niece of Lennie. She is introduced in Ep 115 scouting for demonic presence with a Detection Needle, and is later seized by a demon general, with Zane as her only hope of rescue (Eps 118-119). She corresponds to Zhu Qianning of the Zhu Family in the source novel, a female disciple whose clan is famous for its needle techniques. Both episode pronouns and the source confirm her as female; the brief 'Helen' mislabeling in Eps 201-208 was a localization error that has been corrected.

name: World Merchants' Guild
reason: The source organization 'World Business Alliance' was localized as 'World Merchants' Guild' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: The World Merchants' Guild is the most powerful neutral force in the Heartlands, on par with a sixth-grade sect despite not being a warrior faction. It quietly controls roughly 70% of the vitality mines and 80% of commerce, is led by three Alliance Chiefs (Kieran, Hobbes, and Burns), and hosts the Martial Tournament where Zane makes his name (Eps 418-939). The Guild mediates disputes between factions, maintains Relic-Class treasures in its vault, and administers advanced magic-array tests for entry. It corresponds to the source novel's World Business Alliance, led by Alliance Master Mo Yuezhang.

name: Jacob
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Wang Yun' was fully localized to 'Jacob'; the surname 'Wilson' was assigned to give the personal disciple a complete US-style name (episodes use 'Jacob Wilson' in Eps 235 and 253, 'Jacob' elsewhere).
description: Jacob Wilson is a personal disciple (one of the Sect's Chosen) who becomes a key ally of Zane during the All Peaks Competition arc (Eps 235-315). He is a benchmark genius: three years before the story's tournament he broke into the Top One Hundred while at the same cultivation level Zane holds now. In the competition he fearlessly walks straight into Pu Xingyu's storm of deadly golden threads (Ep 261), a scene matching source chapters 248-249 where Wang Yun, a Hall Master's personal disciple, walks into the 'Sky Snare' net of golden threads while wearing his White Bone Battle Armor. The master sheet records him as 'Jacob Wilson', introduced at Grade Two Adept and progressing significantly through the tournament.

name: Jacob Zane
issues: Extraction artifact: the string 'Jacob Zane' never appears verbatim in the episode text (verified by corpus search); it is noise from adjacent mentions of Jacob and Zane across sentence boundaries.

name: Ethereal Spirit Sect
reason: The source sect 'Void Spirit Sect' was localized as 'Ethereal Spirit Sect' for the Western fantasy register; per the master sheet, 'Ethereal Spirit Order' and a literal 'Void Spirit Sect' rendering are non-canonical.
description: The Ethereal Spirit Sect is the most powerful sect in the Heartlands, a fifth-grade sect whose core members include the stone-faced Septuplets, who fight in perfect battle formation (Ep 454), and whose Brent is a saint/divine-level figure. The sect possesses the Soul Flag, a Relic-Class treasure. Alongside the World Merchants' Guild and Cloud Hall, it is one of the great institutions of the Heartlands era (Eps 423-1042), and its platform fields Inner-Core Realm disciples at major gatherings. It corresponds to the source novel's Void Spirit Sect, a fifth-grade sect noted for having its own Sacred Artifact.

name: Evan
issues: Name reuse: a different, minor 'Evan' (paired with Cole, Lowell trial arc, Eps 40-49) predates this character; the two must not be merged in the sheet.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Li Yifeng' was fully localized to 'Evan', a simple Western name fitting the reclusive, unassuming genius archetype.
description: Evan is the legendary number-one ranked fighter among the Sect's Chosen, the only one ranked above Patrick, and the first-place finisher of the previous All Peaks Competition. Reclusive by nature, he sequesters himself in intensive training and only appears at the very end of the tournament (Eps 316-317), where his airheaded demeanor belies his overwhelming strength. He corresponds to Li Yifeng of the source novel, the first place of the Green Cloud Leaderboard and the Blue Cloud Sect's resident 'monster', who likewise fails to appear until the competition's climax. His episode range (280-367) aligns with Li Yifeng's chapters 267-395.

name: Evan and Cole
issues: Compound fragment, not an entity. Note: the 'Evan' in these early episodes (40-49, a minor Lowell-trial participant alongside Cole and Caleb) is a DIFFERENT character from the famous Evan (Li Yifeng) of Eps 280-367; the name was reused by the localization.

name: Dorothea Garrison
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Gu Pei'er' was fully localized to 'Dorothea'; the surname 'Garrison' was assigned, with her father named Orson Garrison, to create a consistent Western family unit.
description: Dorothea Garrison is an enigmatic, enchantingly beautiful woman of the Talent Pagoda arc (Eps 912-952) who travels with Max's group; her full name and her father, Orson Garrison, are given in Ep 920. Her signature feature is a living flower embedded in her right eye, its roots buried deep in the socket, which spins when she uses her power; with a single effortless move she can sever the soul-core link of master warriors who hijack new bodies, leaving them frozen and helpless (Ep 913). She matches the source novel's Gu Pei'er exactly, down to the spinning flower in her right eye that fires light from its stamen (chs 897-931). Both the episode pronoun signal and the source confirm she is female.

name: Peaks Competition
reason: The source event 'All-Peak Competition' (also 'Peak Competition') was localized as 'All Peaks Competition', keeping the literal meaning while smoothing the phrasing for English narration.
description: The All Peaks Competition is the Skyreach Sect's great inter-peak tournament, contested by roughly 700 fighters drawn from the Thirty-Three Peaks plus the personal disciples. Eligibility requires inner-disciple status, and the event is a career-defining stage: Zane fights his way into it (Eps 188-235) and uses it to announce himself against the sect's elite. It is announced by Sir Kenneth and anchors the Eps 235-320 arc. It corresponds to the source novel's All-Peak Competition of the Blue Cloud Sect, which determines the rankings of the 33 Peaks.

name: Demi-Immortal Race
issues: Episodes use both 'Demi-Immortal Race' (dominant, 30 mentions) and 'Demi-Immortal Clan' (4 mentions, Eps 948-1040) for the same group; recommend standardizing on 'Demi-Immortal Race'.
reason: The source term 'Demi-Immortal Clan' was carried over nearly verbatim as 'Demi-Immortal Race' in the adaptation.
description: The Demi-Immortal Race is a hybrid clan, small in number but extraordinarily powerful and famous for being difficult to deal with. Though its members can appear human, the race stands at the very peak of the universe: its old man ranks alongside the leaders of the three great human powers, the Demon Night's highest authority, and the Ogres' supreme elder (Ep 1185). The race built and once owned the Tower of Sin and the three trial pagodas that grant titles, extending protection to anyone it recognizes, and it eventually places its weight behind Zane, threatening any Supreme Lord who kills him. It corresponds to the source novel's Demi-Immortal Clan/race, whose three pagodas mirror the human race's Heavenly Path and the demon race's Divine-Devil Abyss.

name: Demi-Immortal
reason: The source title 'Demi-Immortal' was carried over verbatim; it names both the top pagoda title and, in the plural, members of the Demi-Immortal Race.
description: 'Demi-Immortal' is the top title earned in the Demi-Immortal Race's trial pagodas, for which the most talented prodigies of every race across a hundred thousand supreme worlds compete (Ep 924). Holders carry the Demi-Immortal mark, which commands instant respect and protection, as Zane and Amber discover (Eps 948-950). In the plural, episodes also use the word for members of the race itself, a diverse group whose relationship with the Ogres is famously terrible. In the source, 'Demi-Immortal was the top title' granted by the three pagodas, making its holder a core member of the Demi-Immortal race.

name: Demi-Immortal Clan
issues: Minor name drift: 'Demi-Immortal Clan' appears in Eps 948-1040 where other episodes say 'Demi-Immortal Race'.

name: Chaos Energy
reason: The source term 'Primal Chaos Qi' was localized as 'Chaos Energy', replacing the Chinese cultivation term 'Qi' with 'Energy' for the Western fantasy register.
description: Chaos Energy is the primordial power Zane cultivates in the late story (Eps 994-1321), an Origin Power from which Vitality itself is believed to have evolved. It amplifies every technique it touches exponentially, but behaves unlike Vitality: it refuses to liquefy even after Zane crosses into Soul Sea territory, forcing him and the Cobalt Dragon to devise ways to let it devour outside Vitality and build its own mass (Eps 1109-1129). A Soul Sea born from Chaos Energy would be a true world rather than a sea of Vitality. It corresponds to the source novel's Primal Chaos Qi, which fills Luo Zheng's dantian and powers his late-stage techniques.

name: Chaos Sea
reason: The source term 'Primal Chaos Sea' was localized as 'Chaos Sea', matching the 'Chaos Energy' rename.
description: The Chaos Sea is the inner sea Zane forms from Chaos Energy in place of an ordinary Sea of Vitality, a fact Gus quickly recognizes as extraordinary (Eps 1129-1224). It corresponds to the Primal Chaos Sea speculated about in the source's Primal Chaos Secret Technique (ch 1109).

name: World Lord
reason: The source rank 'World Lord' was carried over verbatim into the adaptation.
description: World Lord is a late-story power rank (Eps 925-1320) sitting above the Soul Sea Realm and below the Supreme Lords; the universe holds thousands of them, and spells that work on lesser warriors are never supposed to touch beings this powerful. Due to the Dark World's unique history, true World Lords cannot exist there (Ep 1137), while factions like the Demon Night field their own World Lords as enforcers. In the source novel, each of the universe's 100,000 great worlds has its own World Lord, with Great World Lords above them, and the term is used identically.

name: Violet Heart Sanctuary
reason: The source location 'Purple Heart Holy Land' was localized as 'Violet Heart Sanctuary', swapping the literal 'Holy Land' for 'Sanctuary' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: The Violet Heart Sanctuary is the sacred stronghold of the human race on the Sea God Continent, established in the continent's far north by humans, one of the fourteen great races (Eps 560-954). Most of the continent's talented humans come from the Sanctuary, with the rest from smaller allied groups, though it rarely sends its people into the Tower of Sin and is notably weaker than the holy lands of the other races. It corresponds to the source novel's Purple Heart Holy Land, the human-founded Holy Land Luo Zheng encounters on the Sea God Continent.

name: Spirit Supreme Realm
reason: The source realm 'Ultimate God Realm' (also rendered 'Ultimate Divine Realm' in the translation) was localized as 'Spirit Supreme Realm' to slot cleanly above the show's Soul Sea Realm and avoid overloading 'Divine' in the realm ladder.
description: The Spirit Supreme Realm is a late-story cultivation realm (Eps 897-1304) a full level above the Soul Sea Realm: Zane's first duel against a Spirit Supreme master is treated as a milestone (Eps 1118-1120), and even at this realm Lavender once commanded the respect of the Demon Night's Supreme Lords. Its warriors still face long journeys even with teleportation tunnels, marking the scale of the late-story universe. It best matches the source translation's Ultimate God Realm/Ultimate Divine Realm, described as the backbone of the Upper Realm's warriors, whose chapter range (874-1148) aligns with the realm's debut in the episodes.

name: Sir Kenneth
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Shi Jingtian' was fully localized to 'Kenneth', with the honorific 'Sir' replacing his sect-leader form of address for the Western register.
description: Sir Kenneth is the supreme authority of the Skyreach Sect (Eps 235-975). He announces the start of the All Peaks Competition, follows Zane's rise with keen interest, and reveals terrifying power when he kills the fleeing Saint Viana with a single punch from an incredible distance after her faction's treachery is exposed (Eps 278-279). He later allows Elara to come home with Zane, personally prevents Zane's soul from shattering (Ep 348), and worries over the Cloud Road Trial. He corresponds to Shi Jingtian, the Blue Cloud Sect's Sect Leader in the source novel, whose chapter range (222-954) matches Kenneth's episode presence almost exactly.

name: Sir
issues: Generic honorific used for many different characters across Eps 39-1120 (Sir Moon, Sir Kenneth, waiters' customers, the Lord of the Sunset World); not an entity.

name: Sir Kenneth's Vitality
issues: Possessive sentence fragment (one mention, Ep 352), not an entity; its mentions belong to Sir Kenneth.

name: Holy Maiden
reason: The source title 'Saintess' (of the Divine Kingdom, also rendered 'Holy Maiden' in parts of the translation) was localized as 'Holy Maiden', keeping the character's title-as-name convention.
description: The Holy Maiden of the Divine Kingdom is a major rival figure of the Heartlands tournament arc (Eps 492-954), a woman with dark, cold eyes 'like a bottomless lake at midnight' whose destiny is said to be heaven-defying. She competes directly against Zane and Tia in the trials (Eps 541-551), masking storm-dark fury behind giggles when outperformed. She corresponds to the source novel's Saintess/Holy Maiden of the Divine Kingdom, a proud powerhouse covered in opportunities and treasures who swears to raze the Tianbei Region after being humiliated there. Episode pronouns and the source agree she is female.

name: Lowell Manor
reason: The Luo Family's ancestral estate from the source novel was given the Western name 'Lowell Manor', matching the family's localized surname.
description: Lowell Manor is the ancestral home of House Lowell and Bryson's seat of power, where the Blood Prisoner was kept in the cellar. Zane reclaims it during the Eps 324-335 arc, which adapts the Luo Family rebellion chapters (~315-320) of the source.

name: Lowell House
issues: Name drift: 'House Lowell' is the dominant episode form (46 episode files) but 'Lowell House' also appears (7 files); recommend standardizing on 'House Lowell' per the show's 'Legacy House' convention.
reason: The source clan 'Luo Family' (Luo Clan) was localized as 'House Lowell', a Western noble-house construction matching the show's 'Legacy House' terminology; the surname Lowell was chosen to echo 'Luo'.
description: House Lowell is Zane's family, a Legacy House of the Eastern Territory whose ancestral seat is Lowell Manor. In the early episodes the house is a place of cruelty for Zane: dozens of Lowell kids train in its halls, treat slaves as objects, and use Zane as a punching bag, while cousins like Perrin and Andrew Lowell scheme against him (Eps 1-30). Elara Lowell is Zane's sister, and Bryson later rules the house until Zane reclaims it (Eps 324-335). It corresponds to the source novel's Luo Family, an insignificant clan of the Eastern Region's Fengwang Dynasty.
